species.quote: ALEWIFE … Moratorium on River Herring, illegal to possess.

AMERICAN EEL Minimum Size Limit: 9 IN. Possession Limit: 25 per person

BLACK SEA BASS (SEA BASS) Minimum Size Limit: 13 Possession Limit: 15 Season: May 11 through Dec 31
species.notes: Regulations for black sea bass caught in federal waters are subject to change. Please refer to NMFS for regulations in federal waters.

species.quote: BLUEBACK HERRING … Moratorium on River Herring, illegal to possess.

species.limit: 5 per person from shore or a rented or private vessel; 5 per person on for-hire or charter vessels
species.quote: BLUEFISH Minimum Size Limit: None Possession Limit: 5 per person from shore or a rented or private vessel; 5 per person on for-hire or charter vessels

species.size: Minimum Size Limit: 43 inches total length
species.limit: 1 per person, 2 per vessel; whichever is more restrictive
species.quote: COBIA Minimum Size Limit: 43 inches total length Possession Limit: 1 per person, 2 per vessel; whichever is more restrictive Season: June 15 through Sept 20
species.notes: Gaffing is prohibited.

species.limit: 50 per person; additional 50 live bait per customer capacity on for-hire or charter vessels
species.quote: CROAKER Minimum Size Limit: None Possession Limit: 50 per person; additional 50 live bait per customer capacity on for-hire or charter vessels
GREY TROUT (WEAKFISH) Minimum Size Limit: 12 IN. Possession Limit: 1 per person
GROUPERS Minimum Size Limit: None Possession Limit: 1 per person
KING MACKEREL Minimum Size Limit: 27 IN. Possession Limit: 3 per person

species.size: Minimum Size Limit: Min 18 IN. to Max 26 IN.
species.quote: RED DRUM (CHANNEL BASS, REDFISH) Minimum Size Limit: Min 18 IN. to Max 26 IN. Possession Limit: 3 per person
SCUP (PORGY) … Below regulations apply in state waters. Minimum Size Limit: 9 IN. Possession Limit: 30 per person
species.notes: Regulations for Scup (Porgy) caught in federal waters are subject to change. Please refer to NMFS for regulations in federal waters.

species.quote: SHAD, AMERICAN … Illegal to possess American shad.

species.size: Minimum Size Limit: 54 inches fork length; hammerhead sharks 78 inches FL or greater; no minimum for Atlantic Sharpnose, Bonnethead, Blacknose, and Finetooth
species.limit: 1 per vessel (Atlantic Sharpnose and Bonnethead: 1 per person)
species.quote: SHARKS (All species except smooth and spiny dog sharks) Minimum Size Limit: 54 inches fork length ** Possession Limit: 1 per vessel *** … Season Closed May 15 - July 15
species.notes: Recreationally Prohibited Species (illegal to take or possess): Atlantic Angel, Dusky, Sand Tiger, Sandbar, White, and Bigeye Thresher Sharks. All sharks must be landed with head and fins attached. Sharks may only be taken by handline or rod and reel; spearing and bowfishing illegal. No size or possession limits apply to dog sharks.

species.quote: SHEEPSHEAD Minimum Size Limit: None Possession Limit: 4 per person
SPADEFISH Minimum Size Limit: None Possession Limit: 4 per person
SPANISH MACKEREL Minimum Size Limit: 14 IN. Possession Limit: 15 per person
SPECKLED TROUT (SPOTTED SEATROUT) Minimum Size Limit: 14 IN. Possession Limit: 5 per Person, only 1 greater than 24" Season: *Closed April 1 - June 30, 2026

species.limit: 50 per person; additional 50 live bait per customer capacity on for-hire or charter vessels
species.quote: SPOT Minimum Size Limit: None Possession Limit: 50 per person; additional 50 live bait per customer capacity on for-hire or charter vessels

species.season: January 1 through March 31; May 16 through December 31
species.size: Minimum Size Limit: 28 inches; Maximum Size Limit: 31 inches
species.quote: STRIPED BASS (ROCKFISH, STRIPED) Virginia Coastal Seasons January 1 through March 31 May 16 through December 31 Minimum Size Limit: 28 inches Maximum Size Limit: 31 inches Possession Limit: 1 per person
species.notes: Non-offset, corrodible, non-stainless steel circle hooks required when fishing with bait. Gaffing striped bass is illegal in Virginia marine waters. You may not combine possession limits when seasons overlap or you fish in multiple jurisdictions. Coastal regulations apply in the Territorial Sea plus the seaside creeks, bays and inlets of Accomack and Northampton Counties and the City of Virginia Beach.

species.season: Spring: May 16 through June 15; Fall: October 4 through December 31
species.size: Minimum Size Limit: 19 inches; Maximum Size Limit: 24 inches
species.quote: Chesapeake Bay Spring Season Season: May 16 through June 15 Minimum Size Limit: 19 inches Maximum Size Limit: 24 inches Possession Limit: 1 per person / Chesapeake Bay Fall Season Season: October 4 through December 31 Minimum Size Limit: 19 inches Maximum Size Limit: 24 inches Possession Limit: 1 per person
species.notes: Applies in the main stem of the Chesapeake Bay and Virginia Bay tributaries except tributaries of the Potomac River (Potomac River Fisheries Commission rules apply there).

species.quote: Federal water striped bass regulations: Atlantic Ocean waters beyond the 3 mile limit are closed to the taking and possession of striped bass all year.
STURGEON Code Section 28.2-303 Illegal to possess

species.size: Minimum Size Limit January 1-May 31: 16 Inches; June 1-December 31: 17.5 Inches
species.quote: SUMMER FLOUNDER Minimum Size Limit January 1-May 31: 16 Inches Minimum Size Limit June 1-December 31: 17.5 Inches Possession Limit: 4 per person Season: Open year-round
species.notes: Applies to Virginia tidal waters; in Virginia Potomac River tributaries the PRFC mainstem rules apply. Federal-waters rules are set by NMFS.

species.quote: TAUTOG Minimum Size Limit: 16 IN. Possession Limit: 4 per person Season: Closed Season: May 16 - June 30

species.limit: 3 per person on a recreational vessel; 5 per person on a USCG uninspected for-hire vessel; 7 per person on a USCG inspected for-hire vessel
species.quote: TILEFISH, BLUELINE Minimum Size Limit: None Season: May 15 through November 15 … Three (3) fish per person on a recreational vessel; five (5) fish per person on a USCG uninspected for-hire vessel; seven (7) fish per person on a USCG inspected for hire vessel.
TILEFISH, GOLDEN Minimum Size Limit: None Possession Limit: 8 Golden Tilefish per person
Largemouth and Smallmouth Bass: Creel 5 per day in the aggregate (combined); Length: No statewide length limits
species.notes: Clinch River: no bass under 20 inches, 1 per day over 20.

species.quote: Largemouth and Smallmouth Bass: Creel 5 per day in the aggregate (combined)
Alabama and Spotted Bass: No statewide daily limit; No statewide length limit
White Bass: Creel 5 per day; No statewide length limits (South Holston: catch and release only)

species.size: No walleye or saugeye less than 18 inches
species.limit: 5 per day in the aggregate (walleye and saugeye)
species.quote: Walleye and Saugeye: 5 per day in the aggregate; No walleye or saugeye less than 18 inches (Claytor Lake/New River: 2 per day; no walleye 19 to 28 inches)
Sauger: Creel 2 per day; No statewide length limits
Muskellunge: 1 per day; No muskellunge less than 40 inches (New River: 40–48 in protected Jun–Feb; 48 in min Mar–May)
Northern Pike and Chain Pickerel: 5 per day; No statewide length limits
Northern Pike and Chain Pickerel: 5 per day; No statewide length limits
Trout: Creel 6 per day; Length: 7 inch minimum size
species.notes: Stocked and special-regulation trout waters differ (delayed harvest, fly-only, etc.). Trout license required in designated waters.

species.quote: Crappie (Black or White): 25 per day in the aggregate; No statewide length limits (several lakes: 9 or 10 inch minimum)
Bluegill and Other Sunfish: 50 per day in the aggregate; No statewide length limits
Rock Bass and Roanoke Bass: 25 per day in the aggregate; No statewide length limits
Yellow and White Perch: No statewide daily limit; No statewide length limit (Lake Moomaw: 10 per day)
Catfish (Channel, White, Flathead): 20 per day; No length limits (rivers below the fall line: no daily limit)
Catfish (Blue): 20 per day; No statewide length limits (tidal rivers: no limit except 1 per day over 32 inches)

species.limit: July 1 to April 14: 5 per day; April 15 to June 30: 1 per day
species.quote: Longnose Gar and Bowfin: July 1 to April 14: 5 per day; April 15 to June 30: 1 per day
Northern Snakehead: No statewide daily limit; must immediately kill the fish and notify the department

species.season: Hand line, dip net, collapsible traps and cast net: all year. Up to 2 crab pots: March 17 – December 19
species.size: Hard crab 5 inches (male and immature female); mature female (sook) no size limit; peeler 3.25 in Mar 17–Jul 15 and 3.5 in Jul 16–Nov 30; soft crab 3.5 inches
species.limit: 1 bushel of hard crabs and 2 dozen peeler crabs per person per day
species.quote: All recreational crabbing is limited to 1 bushel of hard crabs and 2 dozen peeler crabs per person per day. Minimum sizes (tip to tip of the longest spikes): hard crabs male 5 inches, immature female 5 inches, mature female no size limit; peeler crabs March 17 to July 15 3¼ inches, July 16 to November 30 3½ inches; softshell crabs 3½ inches.
species.notes: March 17 – June 15 only bright orange sponge (egg-bearing) crabs may be kept; brown/black sponge crabs must be returned. VMRC asks that all sponge crabs be released.

species.season: Public oyster season (set each year by area, generally fall and winter); open 7 days a week to hand tongs
species.quote: Taking a maximum of one bushel of oysters in any one day for personal use when taken by hand or with ordinary tongs during the oyster season from open rocks. One bushel per person limit and culling regulations applies.
species.notes: No license needed for personal use from open public grounds by hand or ordinary tongs. Season dates differ by area — see the VMRC public oyster harvest season notice before going.

species.season: Open year-round from areas open to harvest
species.quote: Taking a maximum of 250 clams in any one day for personal use when taken by hand or with ordinary tongs from open areas.
species.notes: By hand or ordinary tongs only; no license needed for personal use. Check VDH condemned-area closures.

species.quote: Kingfish - Minimum Size Limit: No size limit - Recreational Bag Limit: No bag limit
species.notes: MRC main table prints Kingfish (Roundhead) with citation info only; the April 2026 regulation sheet prints no size and no bag limit.

species.quote: DOLPHIN ... Info: SAFMC Dolphin Regulations; Federal Dolphin Regulations
species.notes: Virginia prints no state size, bag or season; it refers anglers to SAFMC and federal (50 CFR 622) dolphin regulations.

species.quote: SWORDFISH ... Info: Managed by NMFS - http://www.hmspermits.gov/
species.notes: Managed by NMFS; HMS permit required.

species.quote: TUNA (BLUEFIN) ... Info: Managed by NMFS - http://www.hmspermits.gov/
species.notes: Managed by NMFS; HMS permit required.

species.quote: TUNA (YELLOWFIN, BIGEYE) ... Info: Managed by NMFS - http://www.hmspermits.gov/
species.notes: Printed together with bigeye tuna; managed by NMFS.

species.quote: TUNA (YELLOWFIN, BIGEYE) ... Info: Managed by NMFS - http://www.hmspermits.gov/
species.notes: Printed together with yellowfin tuna; managed by NMFS.

species.quote: WAHOO ... Info: Managed by SAFMC - http://www.safmc.net/
species.notes: Virginia defers to SAFMC.

species.size: 54 inches fork length; hammerheads 78 inches fork length
species.limit: 1 per vessel per trip (shore angler: 1 per calendar day)
species.quote: E. It shall be unlawful for any person to take, harvest, land, or possess any blacktip, bull, great hammerhead, lemon, nurse, scalloped hammerhead, smooth hammerhead, spinner or tiger shark from May 15 through July 15 of any calendar year. ... D. ... less than 54 inches in fork length ... 1. ... great hammerhead, scalloped hammerhead, or smooth hammerhead shark that is less than 78 inches in fork length. ... A. Recreational fishing vessels are allowed a maximum possession limit of one recreationally permitted shark, excluding smooth dogfish, per trip, regardless of the number of people on board the vessel.
species.notes: Must be landed with head, tail and fins attached; handline or rod and reel only; non-offset corrodible non-stainless circle hooks required except with flies or artificial lures; spearing and bowfishing illegal.

species.limit: 1 per person per trip (vessel) or per calendar day (shore)
species.quote: In addition, each recreational vessel angler may possess one bonnethead and one Atlantic sharpnose per trip. ... 2. Atlantic sharpnose, bonnethead, finetooth, blacknose, and smooth dogfish sharks are exempt from the recreational size limit described in this subsection.
species.notes: In addition to the 1-per-vessel limit on other sharks. Head, tail and fins attached; rod and reel or handline only; circle hooks with bait.

species.limit: 1 per person per trip (vessel) or per calendar day (shore)
species.quote: In addition, each recreational vessel angler may possess one bonnethead and one Atlantic sharpnose per trip. ... 2. Atlantic sharpnose, bonnethead, finetooth, blacknose, and smooth dogfish sharks are exempt from the recreational size limit described in this subsection.
species.notes: In addition to the 1-per-vessel limit on other sharks. Head, tail and fins attached; rod and reel or handline only; circle hooks with bait.

species.limit: 1 per vessel per trip (counts as the vessel's one permitted shark)
species.quote: 2. Atlantic sharpnose, bonnethead, finetooth, blacknose, and smooth dogfish sharks are exempt from the recreational size limit described in this subsection. ... A. Recreational fishing vessels are allowed a maximum possession limit of one recreationally permitted shark, excluding smooth dogfish, per trip
species.notes: No minimum size but still count toward the 1-per-vessel permitted shark limit. Head, tail and fins attached; rod and reel or handline only.

species.quote: "Recreationally permitted shark" means any of the following species: ... Blue, Prionace glauca ... Porbeagle, Lamna nasus ... Thresher, Alopias vulpinus
species.notes: Permitted species not in the May 15 - July 15 closure group. Size and vessel limit from 4VAC20-490-40 D and A. Head, tail and fins attached; rod and reel or handline only.

species.quote: No size or possession limits apply to Dog Sharks. ... All sharks (All species except Spiny Dog Sharks) must be landed with head and fins attached
species.notes: Smooth dogfish must still be landed with head and fins attached; spiny dogfish are exempt from that rule.

species.quote: "Recreationally prohibited shark" means any of the following species: Atlantic angel, Squatina dumeril; Basking, Cetorhinus maximus; Bigeye sand tiger, Odontaspis noronhai; Bigeye sixgill, Hexanchus nakamurai; Bigeye thresher, Alopias superciliosus; Bignose, Carcharhinus altimus; Caribbean reef, Carcharhinus perezii; Caribbean sharpnose, Rhizoprionodon porosus; Dusky, Carcharhinus obscurus; Galapagos, Carcharhinus galapagensis; Longfin mako, Isurus paucus; Narrowtooth, Carcharhinus brachyurus; Night, Carcharhinus signatus; Oceanic whitetip, Carcharhinus longimanus; Sand tiger, Carcharias taurus; Sandbar, Carcharhinus plumbeus; Sevengill, Heptranchias perlo; Shortfin mako, Isurus oxyrinchus; Silky, Carcharhinus falciformis; Sixgill, Hexanchus griseus; Smalltail, Carcharhinus porosus; Whale, Rhincodon typus; White, Carcharodon carcharias
species.notes: 4VAC20-490-40 C: It shall be unlawful for any person to possess any recreationally prohibited shark.

species.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to possess any lobster less than 3-17/32 inches in carapace length or any lobster greater than 5-1/4 inches in carapace length ... E. It shall be unlawful to land lobster from February 1 through March 31. ... A. It shall be unlawful for any person to possess any berried female lobster ... C. ... to possess a V-notched female lobster. D. It shall be unlawful to possess a lobster that has an outer shell that has been speared.
species.notes: No berried (egg-bearing) or V-notched females; no speared lobsters; no detached tails, claws or meat aboard a vessel.

species.limit: 4 per day in the aggregate (striped bass and hybrids combined)
species.quote: Striped Bass - Landlocked Striped Bass and Landlocked Striped Bass X White Bass Hybrids ... 4 per day in the aggregate No fish less than 20 inches
species.notes: Lake exceptions: Buggs Island/Kerr (Oct 1-May 31: 2/day aggregate, 20-26 inch slot; Jun 1-Sep 30: 4/day no length limit); Claytor Lake (Sep 16-Jun 30: 2/day, 20 inch min; Jul 1-Sep 15: 4/day no length limit); Lake Gaston (4/day; Oct 1-May 31 20 inch min; Jun 1-Sep 30 no length limit); Smith Mountain Lake (2/day; Nov 1-May 31 no fish 30-40 inches; Jun 1-Oct 31 no length limit).

species.limit: 25 per day in the aggregate with rock bass
species.quote: Roanoke Bass 25 per day in the aggregate with rock bass No statewide length limits | Nottoway, Meherrin, and Blackwater (Franklin County), Blackwater (Chowan), Falling and Smith rivers and their tributaries | 5 per day in the aggregate (combined) with rock bass No Roanoke bass less than 8 inches
species.notes: Nottoway, Meherrin, Blackwater (Franklin Co.), Blackwater (Chowan), Falling and Smith rivers and tributaries: 5 per day combined with rock bass, no Roanoke bass less than 8 inches.

species.quote: Perch (yellow and white) No statewide daily limit No statewide length limit | Lake Moomaw 10 per day
species.notes: Nongame page: white perch may be possessed in unlimited numbers; may also be taken below the fall line in tidal rivers with a gill net under VMRC recreational rules. Lake Moomaw exception printed for the perch row (10 per day).

species.limit: July 1 to April 14: 5 per day; April 15 to June 30: 1 per day
species.quote: Bowfin July 1 to April 14: 5 per day April 15 to June 30: 1 per day No statewide length limits
species.notes: Bow and arrow allowed in tidal waters (below fall line); bowfin taken by bow must be retained.

species.zone: Virginia inland public rivers and streams (not public lakes/reservoirs)
species.quote: Grass Carp No statewide daily limit No statewide length limit | Anglers may possess grass carp taken from inland public waters, except for public lakes and reservoirs. Anglers must ensure that harvested grass carp are dead.
species.notes: May not be harvested from public lakes and reservoirs (Department-owned or controlled lakes). Must be killed; bow and arrow allowed except in trout-stocked waters; bow-taken fish must be retained.

species.quote: No possession limits - can be possessed in unlimited numbers. Carp, mullet, white sucker, northern hogsucker, gizzard shad, threadfin shad, white perch, yellow perch (10 fish limit in Lake Moomaw), alewife and blueback herring [see limits under Anadromous (coastal) in creel and length limits table], stoneroller (hornyhead), fathead minnow, golden shiner, goldfish, and Asian clams.
species.notes: Bow and arrow (including crossbow) allowed day and night except in trout-stocked waters; bow-taken carp must be retained and not returned to the water.

species.quote: No possession limits - can be possessed in unlimited numbers. Carp, mullet, white sucker, northern hogsucker, gizzard shad, threadfin shad, white perch, yellow perch (10 fish limit in Lake Moomaw), alewife and blueback herring [see limits under Anadromous (coastal) in creel and length limits table], stoneroller (hornyhead), fathead minnow, golden shiner, goldfish, and Asian clams.
species.notes: Gizzard shad and white perch may also be taken below the fall line in Chesapeake Bay tidal rivers by gill net under VMRC recreational rules. Alewife and blueback herring are NOT unlimited - see their own rows (possession banned in coastal rivers).

species.quote: Other native or naturalized nongame fish 20 per day No length limits | Statewide | See pages 27-28 for exceptions
species.notes: Nongame page: 20 - Nongame Fish and Aquatic Invertebrates (personal use). Suckers: 20 per day by dip net (Feb 15 - May 15) or snagging/gigging in listed waters. Bait minnows/chubs/hellgrammites: 50 in aggregate. Crayfish: 20 in aggregate. In designated stocked trout waters nongame fish may be taken only by hook and line Oct 1 - Jun 15.

species.quote: Threatened and endangered species No possession | None apply | None apply
species.notes: Nongame page: No possession allowed. Threatened and endangered species, freshwater mussels, candy darter, eastern hellbender, diamondback terrapin, and spotted turtle. It shall be unlawful to take mussels from any inland waters in Virginia.

species.zone: Meherrin (below Emporia Dam), Nottoway, Blackwater (Chowan), North Landing and Northwest rivers and tributaries, plus Back Bay
species.size: No length limit (Chowan drainage); Chesapeake rivers as set by VMRC
species.limit: 10 per day in the Chowan drainage rivers; Chesapeake Bay coastal rivers as set by VMRC
species.quote: Hickory Shad - Above and below the fall line in all coastal rivers of the Chesapeake Bay and their tributaries: Creel and length limits shall be the same as those set by the Virginia Marine Resources Comm. in tidal rivers | Meherrin River below Emporia Dam, Nottoway River, Blackwater River (Chowan Drainage), North Landing and Northwest rivers, and their tributaries plus Back Bay: 10 per day No length limits
species.notes: VMRC recreational table does not print a hickory shad row; only American shad is listed as illegal to possess.

species.zone: Back Bay and tributaries incl. Lake Tecumseh, and North Landing River and tributaries
species.quote: Southern Flounder - Back Bay and tributaries, including Brinson's Inlet Lake (Lake Tecumseh), and the North Landing River and its tributaries: 6 per day, no fish less than 15 inches
species.notes: DWR rule for Back Bay / North Landing River (inland waters). VMRC does not print a southern flounder row; summer flounder rules apply in VMRC tidal waters.

species.quote: The possession limit for crayfish is 20 in aggregate. Note: Madtoms, crayfish, and salamanders cannot be bought or sold.
species.notes: Cannot be bought or sold. Rusty, Australian and marbled crayfish are non-native species requiring a permit to possess.
